# Card 214: task-force declaration proposal (D153 objection window)

Category: task-force declaration.

## Task force
- Product manager (ready): Claude | why: refines card 214 at ready (folds the second hazard into the three Done checks) and keeps the F-056 closure conditions of window 214-rerank-4 | context: ctx-1
- Architect (slice): Claude | why: slices the card and writes the check-by-layer table (port ownership in GeneratedApi.StartAsync versus the readiness probe) and decides how the bound address is read from the child process | context: ctx-6
- QA engineer (red): Claude | why: writes the ZOMBIES for all three Done checks, including the second hazard (WaitUntilListeningAsync accepting a foreign process), and commits Done check 1 red before any fix | context: ctx-2
- Backend developer [author] (green): Claude | why: changes tests/Phrase.Acceptance.Tests/Support/GeneratedApi.cs (ASPNETCORE_URLS on port 0, bound address read from the process, FreeLoopbackPort removed); covers .NET and Kestrel hosting | context: ctx-3
- Independent reviewer (test-infrastructure and Kestrel hosting lens) [reviewer]: Claude | why: non-author review that no choose-then-release window remains, that the harness still kills only its own PID, and that timeouts and assertions are unchanged | context: ctx-4
- Delivery lead (ship): Claude | why: runs the D154 pre-ship gate and the CI-on-main check, and holds the F-056 closure evidence (removal commit plus a green full acceptance suite in CI on the last commit) | context: ctx-7
- Product manager (signoff): Claude | why: fresh context signs off against the Done checks and the 214-rerank-4 conditions | context: ctx-5

## Left out
UX designer, frontend developer (no interface); database developer (no such code); security (no new trust boundary; loopback only, test harness only); DevOps (no workflow or runner change; CI is only the evidence source, read by the delivery lead); technical writer; language and grammar designers (no language change); performance engineer (startup and stop timeouts unchanged); agile coach (no process change; the missed-red lesson is already recorded with F-056 for the retro); separate .NET/Kestrel expert and separate test-infrastructure expert (see below).

## Domain expert (refinement)
Should another domain join now? No. The change is one harness file (GeneratedApi.cs) plus its tests, using documented Kestrel behaviour (binding port 0 and reporting the address on the "Now listening on:" line). The backend developer seat covers .NET and Kestrel hosting, and the reviewer seat is given the test-infrastructure and Kestrel lens explicitly so the author does not review their own hosting assumptions. If the red seat finds the hosting behaviour differs on Linux CI (for example the listening line or process output differs), any member adds a hosting or CI-runner expert through a Decider (mid-card addition, with the Decider id).

## Reason for Claude seats
Probes at 08:21 UTC (commit a5be583, .mob/records/probes/2026-10-30.jsonl) show Codex, Copilot, Grok and agy without usable quota. Each seat is a distinct fresh context, and nobody reviews or QAs their own increment (author ctx-3, reviewer ctx-4, QA ctx-2, signoff ctx-5).

## Window rule
- Every declared role is polled (F-054): all seven role seats answer, each in its own fresh context.
- Each seat answers either "no objection" or ONE fixed condition (D145). A condition that is simply adopted and re-polled stays in the window; an unsettled objection goes to a full Decider.
- Conditions carried from window 214-rerank-4: 214 starts only after this window polls every declared role and QA has written ZOMBIES for the Done checks; Done check 1 is committed red before the fix; F-056 closes only on git evidence (commit removing FreeLoopbackPort and a green full acceptance suite in CI on 214's last commit). QA's carried note (second-hazard red test) is placed in Done checks 1 and 2 below, not added as a fourth check.

## Why this is neither a one-way door nor a standing-rule change
Two-way door: the declaration ends with the card and can be re-declared; nothing is published, deleted or migrated. It applies TFDD as written and changes no agreement, D-record or checker.


---

# Card 214 text changes (exact replacement lines; stay within 3 Done checks)

Replace Done check 1:
  1. Root cause shown red (two hazards, committed red before the fix): (a) a test holds the port FreeLoopbackPort would return, or forces a chosen port to be taken before the API binds, and the current harness fails with "address already in use"; (b) a test puts a foreign process on the port the harness waits on and the current WaitUntilListeningAsync reports the API as up. ZOMBIES to be written by QA at ready.

Replace Done check 2:
  2. Own the port: the API is started on http://127.0.0.1:0 (or equivalent) and the harness reads the bound address from the process (for example the "Now listening on:" line) instead of FreeLoopbackPort, and readiness is confirmed against that reported address of the process it started, so a foreign listener is never accepted; both red tests turn green. ZOMBIES to be written by QA at ready.

Keep Done check 3 unchanged, and append to it:
  ... and the F-056 closure evidence is the commit removing FreeLoopbackPort plus that green CI run id on the last commit (a single green re-run of fb13e3d does not close it).

Replace "Not in this card":
- **Not in this card:** retries on bind failure (they hide the race rather than remove it); any change to xUnit parallelism; any change to the generated API's product code or Kestrel configuration outside the harness.

Replace the "## Task force" section body:
Declared by objection window 214-taskforce (D153; .mob/records/decisions/214-taskforce.json), roles and contexts as in 214-taskforce-proposal.md.
